title: Replay, Fraud Controls, and Resilience Limits Check

questions.prompt: Which design best applies replay, fraud controls, and resilience limits?
options: Enforce one-time business effects and layered server risk decisions while treating local resilience checks as bypassable signals.
Use root detection as sole authorisation
questions.answer: Enforce one-time business effects and layered server risk decisions while treating local resilience checks as bypassable signals.
questions.explanation: The strongest option enforces authority at the correct boundary and includes limitations, lifecycle, adversarial verification, and recovery.

questions.prompt: A random nonce prevents replay even if the server neither stores nor binds it to identity and payload.
questions.explanation: Blocking every rooted or hook-detected device on the client creates false positives while an attacker can patch the branch or relay through a clean device.

questions.prompt: What makes an operation ID replay-safe?
questions.answer: Server-side atomic storage bound to principal and payload, with defined expiry and repeated-delivery semantics.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the specific security property and boundary required by the lesson rather than naming a library.
